statements: This analysis assumes a single core (R27.5): it is no evidence for a multi-core configuration.

Interference bounds assume the Overrun handling of R18 (R18.9): a Task of a Partition whose Overrun_Response stops overrunning Jobs is charged Budget + Δ_detect + Δ_enforce + its longest Critical_Section; other Tasks are charged their Budget.
Every offset is treated as zero (synchronous release, R29.1); release jitter J_rel applies to every Task.

omitted_terms: Endpoint operations (R40.2, task 21.5) are approximated: for each of the 2 declared Endpoint(s) (program, status) a role's send and receive are Critical_Sections of Δ_send and Δ_recv at the Kernel level in every blocking term, and each role's declared operations per Job (`ops`, 1 unless declared) × the larger of the two is charged in its Task's O_i; the count per Job is the declaration's, not measured, and Δ_send and Δ_recv are the measured maxima over the configuration's payload sizes (R33.2)
no FPU-using Task: Δ_fp_save and Δ_fp_restore are not charged

the Kernel-level work of a lower-Priority Task's arrivals and timed events and of the housekeeping event (R19.2) interferes with every Task in the RTA; the UPPAAL model carries a Task's own in E_j only, on the Tasks the Task's Jobs preempt
UPPAAL export: Critical_Sections and the System_Ceiling are approximated by the blocking interval B_i spent before each Job starts, not by locations that raise the ceiling
UPPAAL export: the Kernel overheads of R29.3 are folded into each Task's execution-time bound E_i, not modelled as locations
